newsitem.title: FRANCE: GAN property sale seen in August - source.
newsitem.headline: GAN property sale seen in August - source.

text.p: The results of a tender of property assets belonging to French state-controlled insurer GAN should be known in August, a source close to the deal said on Friday.
"The results of the tender will be known in the next few weeks, it will be pretty quick now. I think it will be done in the month of August," he said.
The properties are held by GAN's Baticredit. Bankers Trust is handling the auction.

Market sources said there are three bidders in the tender, which was launched in May: Whitehall Street Real Estate LP, a fund managed by Goldman Sachs, General Electric Capital Corp and Morgan Stanley. Lehman Brothers and Wilshire Financial Services Group Inc recently dropped out of the bidding, the sources said.
Lehman Brothers declined to comment and Wilshire was not available for comment.

GAN officials declined to reveal the value of the assets being sold. The company reiterated in May that its objective was to sell 3.8 billion francs of net assets, with a nominal value of 16.9 billion, in the coming months.

The sale of distressed property assets is part of GAN's restructuring plan prior to its privatisation, which the government has undertaken to launch by the middle of next year in return for European Commission approval of a state rescue aid package.

Market sources said they thought the assets being auctioned were worth up to one billion francs, "fairly representative of the property crisis, that's to say, fairly diversified" and of mediocre quality.
"For the most part, they were transactions which went sour," said one source, citing the example of land bought without building permission.
Property investment professionals are particularly interested in this disposal as it is the first large sale of physical assets rather than loans. The assets include shops, offices, land and housing.

"We hope that this sale will start a trend, much like Barclays started the sale of loans," said a source. A sale by Barclays Plc of its French property loan book in December 1995 was followed by similar sales by Cie de Suez, the CDR state-backed holding company and UAP.
